title: Economist Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion with Casual Loading and Super
description: Convert an economist salary from hourly to annual using 38-hour weeks. Includes casual loading, super on top, and tax estimates from Fair Work and ATO.
salarySummary: For a full-time economist on a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How do I convert an economist hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $50/hour × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for quick calculations.

faqs.q: Is casual loading included in the economist salary figures?
faqs.a: No, casual loading is a separate 25% addition on top of the base hourly rate for casual employees. The Fair Work Commission sets the casual loading at 25% of the minimum wage. If you are a casual economist, check the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page to apply the correct rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for an economist salary?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of your gross salary at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For example, on a $100,000 salary, super adds $12,000. The Australian Taxation Office enforces this. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for more.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding an Economist Salary: Hourly to Annual

When you're negotiating an economist salary, it helps to see the full picture: what your hourly rate means as an annual figure, how casual loading can boost your pay, and how superannuation adds value on top. This guide uses the latest Fair Work Commission and Australian Taxation Office figures to give you a clear estimate.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week, the annual gross salary is:

**Hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, an economist earning $60 per hour would have an annual base of $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560. This is the starting point before considering casual loading, super, or tax.

We assume 38 hours because that's the standard full-time week under the National Employment Standards. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust accordingly. Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your exact hours.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you work as a casual economist, you're entitled to a 25% loading on your base hourly rate. This compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. The Fair Work Commission's National Minimum Wage Order 2026 sets the casual loading at 25%.

For a casual economist with a base rate of $60/hour, the casual rate becomes $60 × 1.25 = $75/hour. Annualised: $75 × 38 × 52 = $148,200. Remember, super is still paid on top of this amount.

**Important:** Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into our calculator. Use the base hourly rate, then check the casual loading box to add the 25% correctly.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings (2026–27 rate). This is on top of your gross salary, not deducted from it. The Australian Taxation Office oversees this requirement.

For the economist earning $118,560 base, super adds $14,227.20 per year (12% of $118,560). However, the maximum contribution base is $270,830, so super stops accruing once your earnings exceed that threshold.

### Tax Estimates for 2026–27

Tax is deducted from your gross salary, not from super. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on the next $26,800 (to $45,000)
- 30% on the next $90,000 (to $135,000)
- 37% on the next $55,000 (to $190,000)
- 45% above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). For a $118,560 salary, tax plus Medicare would be roughly $28,000–$30,000, depending on your circumstances. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Where Does an Economist Salary Sit?

Economist salaries vary widely by experience, sector, and location. While we don't have a precise figure from the search results, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adults at $2,083.70 (May 2026). Many professional economists earn above this average. For comparison, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week.

If you're covered by an award or enterprise agreement, check the specific rates. Our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) can help.

### Fortnightly and Monthly Views

Sometimes it's useful to see your economist salary per fortnight. Multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the $60/hour economist:

- Weekly: $60 × 38 = $2,280
- Fortnightly: $2,280 × 2 = $4,560
- Annual: $2,280 × 52 = $118,560

Super is typically paid each payday under the new Payday Super rules from 1 July 2026.

### Important Disclaimer

This estimate assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a deeper dive, see our [about the timesheet](/about) page or explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) trends.
